title: Decision Helix: Guided Rollout Microflow Prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
body: Purpose: prototype a compact, decision-first rollout composer for the Redwood Console that helps PMs and SREs create canary/A-B traffic splits with clear rollback triggers and a visible cost/latency trade-off. The "Decision Helix" is a layered microflow: linear timeline at top, progressive allocation ribbon in the middle, and a vertical decision rail on the right summarizing automated guardrails and rollback confidence. This ticket covers high-fidelity screens, an interactive Figma prototype for user testing, and a short dev handoff spec for engineering prioritization.
design_notes: Key UX patterns: 1) Decision-first defaults: surface a recommended 3-step canary (0->5->20->100) with safety gates baked in. 2) Helix visualization: use concentric ribbons to show historical runs and simulated outcomes for each ramp step. 3) Rollback confidence score: compute from realtime signals (error rate, latency z-score, user impact) and translate to a single, explainable badge. 4) Cost heatline: small inlined sparkline next to each step showing estimated per-minute $ impact. 5) Keyboard-first micro-editor: allow power users to edit percentages and durations without opening modal. 6) Accessibility: ensure contrast of ribbons, alt text for simulation overlays, and focus states for keyboard traversal. Trade-offs: compactness vs. discoverability — we prioritize minimal friction for repeatable canaries at the expense of deep custom policy composition (that remains in advanced mode).
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates create/edit/delete of a 3-step canary and 'emergency rollback' flow
Usability test (n=6) shows >80% users can configure a canary and enable automatic rollback in under 3 minutes
Design tokens and component variants included in handoff spec (buttons, ribbons, badges, tooltips)
Engineering acceptance: initial API contract for rollouts validated with ENG-2891
Performance consideration documented: estimated incremental telemetry queries and suggestion to cache simulation runs
comments: 2025-01-08 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff — mapped current console pain points from PM interviews; sketched three layout options (timeline-first, ribbon-first, decision-rail-first). Decided to prototype a compact, decision-first layout for quicker ramp creation.
2025-01-09 - Liam Chen: Reviewed initial wireframes; requested an inline cost estimate per step and keyboard editing. Flagged dependency on ENG-2891 for rollout API support.
2025-01-10 - Ben O'Connor (PM): Added customer scenario 'frequent small experiments' and requested A/B split templates. Suggested 'fast fail' preset for aggressive rollback thresholds.

2025-01-11 - Design critique: team preferred helix ribbon for historical context; noted potential confusion with color encoding — agreed to add legend and use texture patterns for color-agnostic accessibility.
2025-01-12 - UX Research (Maya Patel): Scheduled 6 remote moderated sessions for 2025-01-16; test script drafted to validate microflow and emergency rollback mental model.
2025-01-13 - Liam Chen: Uploaded developer handoff doc and initial component list. Called out need for simulated traffic runner (ENG-3045) to power prototype simulations.

2025-01-14 - Ava Martinez: Implemented feedback; added rollback confidence tooltip with detailed signal breakdown and linked to observability dashboard mock (latency, errors, cost). Marking design ready for engineering feasibility review.
review_feedback: PM Review (Ben): love the recommended defaults; request adding an 'audience freeze' option to pause rollouts for specific cohorts.
Eng Review (Priya Rao): feasibility OK; we need a small backend signal adaptor to compute rollback confidence — suggested a scoped endpoint returning score + signal breakdown.
Security (Tom Blake): requested that audit log events include step-level metadata and 'who triggered rollback' details; flagged retention requirement for compliance customers.
Accessibility (Samira Khan): advise adding texture patterns to ribbons for colorblind support and verifying keyboard order for the decision rail.
Design Ops (Nora Li): asked to include new ribbon component variants in the design system with tokenized spacing and color variables.
next_steps: Finalize Figma prototype after usability sessions (due 2025-01-18)
Sync with ENG-2891 & ENG-3045 for API contract and simulation runner (meeting 2025-01-16)
Add 'audience freeze' option and update handoff spec for audit log fields
Create a small acceptance test plan for the emergency rollback path
